Theme 032 · Light, optics & texture

Risograph Two-Drum Print

Uncoated paper, two semi-transparent riso inks (teal and fluorescent coral), coarse halftone dots and a few pixels of misregistration, moving like a flip-book at 12 fps. The first drum prints your dashboards; Acme Pulse is the second drum, a coral pass that lands only where something is wrong.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Paper + grain — warm uncoated stock with an SVG feTurbulence speckle multiplied over everything.
  • Halftone field — SVG dot patterns: teal at 45°, coral at 15°, dot size carries the value.
  • Misregistered headline — two stacked copies (teal, coral) in multiply, 3–8 px apart.
  • Crop marks + colour bar — printer furniture that says "this is a physical proof".
  • Flag stamp — circular coral stamp with ring text; the agent's signature on the anomaly.
  • Overprint button — coral block with an off-register teal outline; the human action.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Plate-by-plate build — teal drum prints, coral lands 4 frames later; everything stepped at 12 fps (steps(n)), so each plate hit sits on an 8th note at 120 BPM.
  • Registration wobble — the coral layer drifts 1–2 px per frame from a seeded offset table; subtle, constant, never random.
  • Dot-grow reveal — halftone radius 0→full, power2.out over 0.5 s (one beat), like ink soaking into paper.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

"The second pass only prints what's wrong" is a crisp, physical metaphor for an agent that audits quietly on top of your data. Risk: the zine texture can read as playful; keep type strict and numbers in mono.

Adapt to your product: Print your own table or dashboard as plate 1 and let plate 2 hit only the rows your product flags; the stamp text becomes your status label.
